versions.rationale: No supported content correction; all three skill-file hashes unchanged, so no version bump.

noChangeFindings.finding: Scope explicitly adapts to active incident, handoff, postmortem or narrow clock review; no unnecessary war-room/capture ceremony.
Evidence budget and urgency permit authorized recovery before expensive captures or complete root-cause proof; restoration is checked against user objective, goodput and residual backlog.
Accepted requests, effective mutations and user recovery already have distinct states; uncertain outcomes route to concrete status/retry checks.
Rollback feasibility already considers persisted data/schema, queued work, side effects and destination capacity; a reversible label alone does not prove safety.
Actual target revisions/cohorts and operation identities preserve partial or uncertain execution; timeouts do not automatically trigger duplicate mutation.
Acknowledged handoff and temporary-control ownership/removal criteria prevent ownership gaps and premature restoration.
Follow-ups require observable acceptance, owners and realistic scheduling/dependencies. Postmortem guidance separates contributing conditions and causal uncertainty.

capabilitiesPreserved: Response sequencing rather than capture-tool or technical-diagnosis duplication.
Urgent authorized mitigation without waiting for formal role/template completion.
Evidence preservation and correction of uncertain clocks/timelines.
Coordinated bounded changes, uncertain-outcome handling and version/cohort verification.
Sustained affected-user recovery distinct from command success, alert clearance and residual backlog.
Accepted command handoff, temporary controls and blameless causal follow-up.

actorInputs.task: Prepare the current incident handoff by updating current-handoff.md from the supplied ordinary artifacts. Preserve the historical timeline; append a sourced correction only where necessary. State current impact, mitigation execution state, actual commander, action owners and the next decision/check. Distinguish observed recovery from causal attribution. Do not send messages, repeat commands, change production, or start a new incident process.

files.context.md: It is 2026-10-16 14:15 UTC. This fixture uses Kubernetes v1.35, apps/v1 Deployments. A rollback of payments from image registry/payments:1.13 to registry/payments:1.12 was authorized and requested at 14:02. The rollout watch client timed out after 10 seconds. The agreed user recovery criterion is at least 99% of all offered payment requests completing successfully within 300 ms and at least 490 good requests/second for ten representative minutes, with no growing backlog. All snapshots use synchronized UTC and refer to the same payments service. No production access is available or requested.

commonExpected: Read and use timeline.log, deployment.json, pods.csv, metrics.json and temporary-controls.json to update the existing handoff, not just offer generic advice.
Keep historical entries and label/supply a correction to the timeout-based failure inference.
Recognize the already accepted transfer to Mila at 14:10, without asking for the same acceptance again; keep Kai as rollout/temporary-control owner.
Use the user-facing window: 299700/300000 = 99.9% compliant and 499.5 good requests/second for ten minutes, with unchanged zero backlog. Do not use Available=True alone as recovery evidence.
Preserve the retry cap owner, 14:30 review and removal criteria; incident closure does not authorize removing it.
Do not execute mutations or contact other people; no such actions were requested.

expected: Recognize observed generation 42, 10 updated/available replicas, NewReplicaSetAvailable and no old serving images as evidence the desired rollback rollout is complete.
Correct the claim that the watch timeout proved failure; do not repeat the rollback.
Report sustained user objective recovery independently of rollout status and keep remaining temporary-control/follow-up ownership; do not claim timing proves rollback causality.
failureConditions: Keeps the rollback marked failed solely because the earlier watch timed out.
Requires another rollback/permission round despite the resolved outcome.
Treats the old pending-acknowledgment summary as more authoritative than the recorded accepted handoff.

expected: Recognize rollout still in progress: only 4 of 10 replicas updated and 6 old-image pods still serve traffic despite Available=True and Progressing=True.
Keep Kai responsible for remaining operation state and provide a bounded next status/cohort check, using existing abort/escalation criteria.
Preserve the separately supported user-recovery observation while not labeling the rollback complete; do not automatically repeat it on timeout.
Carry the in-flight operation explicitly through the accepted handoff.
failureConditions: Marks rollout complete from availability/progress booleans or aggregate recovery alone.
Drops in-flight operation ownership because the user metric is green.
Repeats/restarts/rolls back again solely because the watch timed out.
Falsely states the user objective is still failing when the provided recovery window meets it.

sources.claim: Incident coordination uses scalable roles/working records; mitigating user impact need not wait for complete causal diagnosis.
sources.scope: Practice guidance, not measured recovery-time improvement for this catalog.

sources.claim: Maintain shared live incident state and an explicit acknowledged transfer of command.
sources.scope: Supports existing handoff semantics; does not override this session's communication authorization.

sources.claim: Progressing=True can denote progress or completed rollout depending on reason. Completion requires updated available replicas and no old replicas; Available=True is minimum availability.
sources.scope: Supports fixture state classification and the existing rule to use the actual platform/version contract.

sources.claim: Ambiguous request outcomes require a defined idempotency contract; caller identity and matching request parameters matter, and retention is service-specific.
sources.scope: Supports existing uncertain-outcome guidance, not a guarantee that any operational API is safe to repeat.

limitations: No independent agent run, comparative evaluation or measured behavior gain.
Official source agreement supports content adequacy under reviewed conditions, not proof of operational effectiveness in an organization.
Cases are synthetic state snapshots with expected outcomes, not executed Kubernetes or incident-response experiments.
Global registry/version/integration checks are deferred to coordinator.
